company__culture__all-remote__meetings.md:16:1. **Use "speedy meetings."** This [Google Calendar setting](https://calendar.google.com/calendar/r/settings) creates meetings of 25 / 50 minute duration, which leaves time to write notes, stretch, etc. in between meetings.
company__culture__all-remote__meetings.md:17:1. **Use the Zoom scheduler plug-in to add video conferencing to your Google Calendar event.** Leveraging the Zoom plug-in automatically adds Zoom links to your event, and reduces the probability of user error in copying and pasting an incorrect video conferencing link.
company__culture__all-remote__meetings.md:108:[Omitted long matching line]
company__culture__all-remote__meetings.md:111:Managers can support their direct reports by reviewing the directs' calendars with them on a regular basis to align on which meetings should have in-person attendance.
company__culture__all-remote__meetings.md:117:[Omitted long matching line]
company__culture__all-remote__meetings.md:123:When scheduling a meeting at GitLab, we value people's time and prefer the "speedy meetings" setting in our Google Calendar. This gives us meetings of, for example, 25 or 50 minutes - leaving some time to write notes, stretch, etc. before continuing to our next call. Learn more in the [Communication section of GitLab's Handbook](/handbook/communication/#scheduling-meetings).
company__culture__all-remote__meetings.md:127:"[No agenda, no attenda](/handbook/communication/#external-communication)." Every work-related meeting should have a single live doc agenda affixed to the calendar invite at the time that the invite is added to calendars.
company__culture__all-remote__meetings.md:158:1. For action items, we [go directly to a GitLab issue](/handbook/communication/#start-with-a-merge-request) or [merge request](https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/user/project/merge_requests/). This creates a direct takeaway from the meeting, where ideas are summarized and action can begin immediately. Be sure to add a link the issue or MR in your meeting agenda for reference and completeness.
company__culture__all-remote__meetings.md:205:### 9. It's OK to look away
company__culture__all-remote__meetings.md:209:1. It's completely acceptable to work on other tasks if (a particular portion of) a meeting doesn't apply to you. If your meeting is with only GitLab team members please leave your camera on to allow people to see the overall interest level and adjust the time spent on certain topics. If your meeting includes non-GitLab team members consider turning off your camera because people outside GitLab might not know that it is acceptable for us to work on other tasks during a meeting.
company__culture__all-remote__meetings.md:240:1. Review your calendar at least a day in advance of the meeting, so that you are aware of the meeting and what is being discussed. Meetings should not be surprises. When people know what is on their calendars and are aware of related materials, they can make smart decisions around how much time to spend reviewing materials in advance.
company__culture__all-remote__meetings.md:241:1. Prepare for your meeting by carefully reading the live doc agenda attached to the calendar invite **before** the meeting. Here's an [example](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1WQe-0oiMCzB3MPBNdKluCEIfgTRpaIi-SJ8FmUJ2xHo/edit?usp=sharing) of what one might look like.
company__culture__all-remote__meetings.md:272:1. Block off everyone's calendar just as if they'd traveled for an offsite. Remove all other distractions (Slack, email, etc.) and enable Do Not Disturb modes on phones and computers.
communication___index.md:137:1. Discussion in issues or Merge Requests is preferred over everything else. If you need a response urgently, you can Slack someone with a link to your comment on an issue or merge request, asking them to respond there, however be aware that they still may not see it straight away. See [Slack](/handbook/communication#slack) for more.
communication___index.md:145:1. All company data should be **shareable** by default. Do not use a local text file, but rather leave comments on an issue.
communication___index.md:229:   1. Lastly, reach out 1-on-1 to stragglers while being respectful of vacation time.
communication___index.md:248:Indicate your availability by updating your own calendar using Google's ["out of office"](https://www.theverge.com/2018/6/27/17510656/google-calendar-out-of-office-option) feature and include the dates you plan to be away in your automated response. Note that this feature will automatically decline any meeting invitations during the time frame you select.
communication___index.md:250:1. Put your planned away time including holidays, vacation, travel time, and other leave in your own calendar. Please see [Communicating your time off](/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/time-off-types/) for more.
communication___index.md:251:1. Set your working hours in your Google Calendar settings.
communication___index.md:252:1. Utilize Time Off by Deel to keep other GitLab team members aware of your [planned time away](/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/time-off-types/) within Slack.
communication___index.md:269:[Omitted long matching line]
communication___index.md:275:1. Do not leave MRs open for a long time. MRs should be **actionable** -- stakeholders should have a clear understanding of what changed and what they are ultimately approving or rejecting.
communication___index.md:287:1. If a project requires multiple approvals to accept your MR, feel free to assign multiple reviewers concurrently. This way the earliest available reviewer can start right away rather than being blocked by the preceding reviewer.
communication___index.md:302:1. When **closing** an issue leave a comment explaining why you are closing the issue and what the MVC outcome was of the discussion (if it was implemented or not).
communication___index.md:304:[Omitted long matching line]
communication___index.md:441:[GitLab Executive Business Administrators](/handbook/eba/) sometimes support teams by taking notes. Since note taking takes time away from their other activities and can often be done by other folks, consider the following before engaging an EBA in a meeting solely for note taking purposes.
communication___index.md:464:1. At the end of the meeting, clearly capture key takeaways, next steps, and [DRIs](/handbook/people-group/directly-responsible-individuals/#what-is-a-directly-responsible-individual).
communication___index.md:523:   - No agenda is required for [coffee chats](/handbook/company/culture/all-remote/informal-communication/#coffee-chats). Note that only meetings that are primarily social in nature should be labeled as a coffee chat in the calendar invite.
communication___index.md:532:[Omitted long matching line]
communication___index.md:533:1. If you want to check if a team member is available for an outside meeting, create a calendar appointment and invite the team member only after they respond yes. Then invite outside people.
communication___index.md:534:1. When scheduling a call with multiple people, invite them using a Google Calendar that is your own, or one specific to the people joining, so the calendar item doesn't unnecessarily appear on other people's calendars.
communication___index.md:535:1. If you want to move a meeting just move the calendar appointment instead of reaching out via other channels. Note the change at the top of the description.
communication___index.md:536:1. Please click 'Guests can modify event' so people can update the time in the calendar instead of having to reach out via other channels. You can configure this to be checked by default under [Event Settings](https://calendar.google.com/calendar/r/settings).)
communication___index.md:537:1. When scheduling a meeting we value people's time and prefer the "speedy meetings" [setting in our Google Calendar](https://calendar.google.com/calendar/r/settings). This gives us meetings of, for example, 25 or 50 minutes leaving some time to:
communication___index.md:543:1. When scheduling a meeting, please try to have it start at :00 (hour) or :30 (mid-hour) to leave common start times available for other meetings on your attendees' calendars. Meetings should be for the time needed, so if you need 15 minutes just book that.
communication___index.md:544:1. When creating a calendar event that will be used company wide, [please place it on the GitLab Team Meetings Calendar](/handbook/tools-and-tips/#gitlab-team-meetings-calendar). That way the event is easily located by all individuals.
communication___index.md:546:1. If you want to schedule a meeting with a person not on the team please use [Calendly](/handbook/tools-and-tips/other-apps/#calendly). Use Google Calendar directly if scheduling with a GitLab team member.
communication___index.md:599:name them after the topic, appended with a session number based on the order they show up in the calendar.
communication___index.md:600:Team members will see the meeting invites in their email or calendar in relation to their local time zone and can decide for themselves which session to attend, based on their working hours.
communication___index.md:638:   - Results come first. Your appearance, location and background is less important than making customers successful so don't wait for the perfect time / place when you can engage a customer right away.
communication___index.md:642:1. Google Calendar also has a [Zoom plugin](https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/zoom-scheduler/kgjfgplpablkjnlkjmjdecgdpfankdle?hl=en-US) where you can easily add a Zoom link for a video call to the invite.
communication___index.md:720:- Trouble seeing details in screen sharing since the screen is further away from them
communication___index.md:749:[Omitted long matching line]
communication___index.md:789:1. The title of every slide should be the message you want the audience to take away, not the subject matter. So use 'Our revenue more than doubled' instead of 'Revenue growth'.
communication___index.md:797:1. When giving a presentation, your commentary should not be a regurgitation of the words in the slide. The audience can read the slide for themselves; your commentary should focus on the most important takeaways.
communication___index.md:852:1. GitLab operates on a [Fiscal Year](/handbook/finance/#fiscal-year) offset from the calendar year. When referring to a fiscal year or quarter, please use the following abbreviations:
communication___index.md:854:   1. "Q1" = the first quarter of the current Fiscal Year, so on Feb 1, 2020, "Q1" is the period from Feb. 1, 2020 through April 30, 2020. Note that Epics in GitLab follow Calendar Years and Quarters.
communication___index.md:1055:1. Use the `:white_check_mark:` emoji or similar to indicate an inquiry has been answered. Anyone can add the emoji. If you're not sure, then feel free to leave it up to the person who asked. An emoji indicator is particularly helpful in channels where lots of questions are posted, such as `#questions`, and `#git-help`.
communication___index.md:1060:1. If you agree in a message to start a video call (typically by asking "Call?") the person that didn't leave the last comment starts the call. So either respond to the "Call?" request with a video link or say "Yes" and let the other person start it. Do not say "Yes" and start a call 5 seconds later since it is likely you'll both be creating a video call link at the same time.
communication___index.md:1092:Consider whether the conversation can take place in a public channel. If not, please use a private channel instead. This channel may have a short-term purpose. It is acceptable to leave the channel and/or archive it if you are no longer an active participant or the channel is no longer in use.
